title: How to Prepare a PDF for Printing

author: The MY PDF FIX Team
body:
## Begin with the destination, not a conversion preset

A PDF's page size is separate from the paper selected in a printer dialog. A landscape page, a cropped scan and an image-sized PDF can all print differently when “fit” or “actual size” is chosen. First find out what the recipient or printer requires: paper size, orientation, margins, color and whether printing is single- or double-sided.

PDF Fix Hub can help with page order, margins, rotation and visible numbering. It is not a professional prepress system: it does not provide PDF/X validation, bleed controls, CMYK conversion, output-intent setup or a guarantee of print-provider acceptance. Ask a commercial printer for its specification before changing a production file.

## Practice: inspect portrait and landscape pages

Download the [print practice PDF](/samples/print-practice.pdf). It contains an A4-sized portrait page and an A4-sized landscape page, both with harmless labels.

1. Open the PDF in your reader and check the document's page dimensions, not just the zoom percentage.
2. Open print preview and select the intended paper size. Compare “actual size” with “fit” to understand scaling.
3. Check whether the landscape page will rotate automatically or use a separate paper orientation.
4. Print one test sheet if practical. Confirm that labels, small type and edge content are visible before printing a whole packet.
5. Keep a copy of the original and note the settings that produced the acceptable test sheet. Different drivers can use different labels and defaults.

These are inspection steps, not a claim that this sample has been tested on your printer.

## Correct orientation without rasterizing unnecessarily

[Rotate PDF](/rotate-pdf) applies the selected 90-, 180- or 270-degree turn to every page in a file. It does not straighten a slightly tilted scan. For a single sideways page, follow the [selective rotation guide](/guides/rotating-scanned-pdfs) rather than rotating unrelated pages.

Do not turn a deliberately landscape chart upright merely to make all thumbnails match. The correct orientation is the one that makes its contents readable on the intended sheet.

## Make room and finalize sequence

[Add Margin](/add-margin-to-pdf) enlarges each page around the existing content. For example, 36 points is half an inch. It does not shrink the content or force the result onto A4. A subsequent “fit” print setting may scale the whole enlarged page, so inspect preview again.

[Crop PDF](/crop-pdf) changes visible boundaries rather than securely removing underlying material. Do not use it to hide confidential content. If duplex printing needs a separator, [Add Blank Page](/add-blank-page-to-pdf) inserts one page at a chosen position; position 0 means before the first page, and its size follows the document's first page.

Finish merging, removing and ordering pages before [adding page numbers](/add-page-numbers-to-pdf). Keep an unnumbered master because another numbering pass adds more page content rather than replacing the old numbers.

## Common mistakes and troubleshooting

Printing grayscale does not guarantee use of only black ink. Choose a black-only mode in the driver if available. [Grayscale PDF](/grayscale-pdf) changes page appearance and rasterizes text; consider the consequences before applying it to a searchable document.

If filled form values disappear in a particular printing workflow, inspect a copy made with [Flatten PDF](/flatten-pdf). Form-only flattening differs from the Everything mode, which renders pages as images. Flattening does not lock a file or make it securely redacted.

## Frequently asked questions

**Will 300 dpi always print perfectly?** No. Rendering resolution cannot restore source detail, and printers and document content vary.

**Why is my converted photo PDF an unusual size?** Image converters use pixel dimensions as PDF points; read [the image conversion workflow](/blog/convert-jpg-and-png-images-to-pdf) before assuming A4 output.

**Should I compress before printing?** Only after inspecting the tradeoff. Strong compression may lose fine detail and selectable text. Use a test print and keep the original.
